title: Processed-16S rRNA Gene Amplicon Sequencing, Physicochemical, and PAH Attenuation Data from Animal Manure-Amended Crude Oil Sludge Co-Composting Microcosms: Bacterial Community Profiles, Diversity Indices, and Functional Pathway Predictions.
author: Onyedikachi Ubani
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0

steps.instruction: This dataset contains all primary, processed, and supplementary data files supporting the manuscript entitled "Dataset Characterising Dominant Bacterial Phylotypes Across Animal Manure-Enriched Composting Microcosms for Crude Oil Sludge Bioremediation", submitted to Data in Brief (Elsevier). The dataset is associated with NCBI BioProject accession PRJNA794053, under which all raw paired-end Illumina MiSeq amplicon sequencing FASTQ files are archived. The experimental system comprised five laboratory co-composting microcosms constructed from crude oil petroleum refinery sludge (sourced from Durban, KwaZulu-Natal Province, South Africa) amended with four animal manures — cow, swine/pig, horse, and poultry — obtained from the University of Pretoria Farm, Pretoria, Gauteng Province, South Africa, plus one unamended control treatment. Each treatment was replicated three times and incubated for 300 days under controlled aerobic conditions at 22 ± 2 °C. Bacterial community composition was profiled by Illumina MiSeq paired-end sequencing (2 × 300 bp, v3 chemistry) of the V1–V3 hypervariable regions of the 16S rRNA gene using universal primers 27F/518R. Raw sequencing reads were quality-filtered using ngsShoRT, chimera-checked with UCHIME, and clustered into operational taxonomic units (OTUs) at 97% sequence similarity using the Mothur pipeline (v1.40.0) aligned against the SILVA database (releases 128 and 132). A total of 125,972 high-quality reads resolved into 359 genera spanning 17 phyla, 42 classes, 83 orders, and 162 families across the five treatments, with Good's coverage exceeding 98% in all samples. The dataset package includes: (i) OTU count tables and relative abundance matrices at phylum, class, order, family, and genus levels; (ii) thirteen alpha diversity indices per treatment (Chao1, Shannon H′, Simpson 1–D, dominance D, Pielou's equitability J, Brillouin, Menhinick, Margalef, Fisher's α, Berger–Parker, evenness eH/S, Brillouin, and Good's coverage); (iii) Bray–Curtis dissimilarity matrices; (iv) PERMANOVA, ANOSIM, and PERMDISP multivariate statistical outputs; (v) PICRUSt2-predicted MetaCyc pathway abundances and KEGG Ortholog (KO) tables for 412 predicted pathways and 7,160 KOs; (vi) PAH compound-specific initial and residual concentrations (mg kg⁻¹) and percentage removal values across 18 PAH compounds spanning 2–6 aromatic rings, quantified by automated Soxhlet extraction/GC–MS over 300 days; (vii) animal manure physicochemical characterisation data (TOC, TON, TOP) and garden soil elemental composition (ICP-OES); (viii) culture-dependent isolation records including 2,6-DCPIP redox scores and catechol 2,3-dioxygenase (cbzE) PCR results; (ix) all R scripts and bioinformatic workflow files used for data processing, statistical analysis, and visualisation; and (x) all manuscript figures in high-resolution TIFF format and all data tables in Excel (.xlsx) and comma-separated value (.csv) formats. The dataset enables reuse in comparative microbial community ecology, compost-based bioremediation protocol development, functional metagenome prediction benchmarking, PAH kinetic modelling, and organic-amendment biostimulation framework design across analogous petroleum-contaminated environmental matrices. Associated BioProject: NCBI BioProject PRJNA794053 Associated Journal: Data in Brief, Elsevier Geographic origin of samples: Durban, KwaZulu-Natal (crude oil sludge); Pretoria, Gauteng (animal manures); Tembisa, Gauteng — S 26°1′0″, E 28°14′0″ (garden soil) Institution: Department of Environmental Sciences, University of South Africa (UNISA), Florida Campus, Roodepoort, Gauteng, South Africa Funding: South African National Research Foundation (NRF), PhD Research Grant Licence: CC BY 4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International)
